desc:
The array nums is sorted in non-decreasing order. Count the negative numbers and count the positive numbers (zero is neither), and return the larger of the two counts.

An O(log n) solution exists; scanning the whole array is not required.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Counting with a loop is O(n). The sorted order says all negatives come first, then zeros, then positives.
The number of negatives equals the index of the first element that is ≥ 0.
The number of positives equals n minus the index of the first element that is > 0. Both indices come from a lower-bound style binary search.
editorial: Because the array is sorted, the negatives form a prefix, the zeros a middle block, and the positives a suffix. Let a be the first index with nums[a] ≥ 0: there are exactly a negatives. Let b be the first index with nums[b] > 0: there are n - b positives.

Each of a and b is a standard boundary search on a monotone condition, so the answer max(a, n - b) costs O(log n). Many zeros do not matter, because the two boundary searches skip the whole zero block.
